title: Personal Checking: electronic-transaction disputes, provisional credit and its reversal
content:
## Scope

This policy governs disputes a Personal Checking owner files about electronic debits: which debits qualify, the notice window, when a provisional credit is owed, and what happens when the dispute is resolved. The notice window, the two provisional credit deadlines and the new-account period are each tier's own published figures.

## Which debits qualify

An electronic-transaction dispute is a claim the owner files about a debit made by domestic debit card purchase, international debit card purchase, withdrawal at a PCB ATM, withdrawal at a non-PCB ATM in the United States, withdrawal at an ATM outside the United States, ACH debit or Zelle payment. Paid checks, wires and official checks are outside this process. The claim is registered with dispute status submitted and a notice date equal to the day the owner gave notice.

## Notice window

The notice must reach PCB within the tier's notice window, in calendar days, after the disputed item posted. The clock starts from the disputed item's posted date on the account; count calendar days with the day after that posted date as day 1; the notice qualifies when the notice date is on or before that posted date plus the notice window, and the boundary day qualifies.

## When the provisional credit is owed

1. A provisional credit is owed when the dispute is still submitted once the tier's provisional credit deadline, in business days, has passed after the owner gave notice.
2. Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Federal Reserve holidays. Count business days with the first business day after the notice date as day 1; the credit is due when the current date is on or after the business day that ends the count.
3. When the account was opened fewer than the new-account period's calendar days before the notice date, the new-account deadline replaces the standard deadline.
4. Only a dispute whose status is submitted can receive a provisional credit, and each dispute receives at most one provisional credit.

## Retired clause

> **No longer in force:** "The provisional credit amount is the dispute's claimed amount, but never more than the disputed item's amount."

This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for the provisional credit amount. The other clauses of this policy remain in force.

## After resolution

| Dispute outcome | Provisional credit | Overdraft fees on the disputed item |
|---|---|---|
| Resolved in the bank's favor | May be reversed, for the full provisional credit amount, against the provisional credit entry | — |
| Withdrawn | May be reversed, for the full provisional credit amount, against the provisional credit entry | — |
| Resolved in the customer's favor | Becomes final with no new entry | Every overdraft item fee tied to the disputed item is refunded, recorded as dispute final |

A provisional credit may be reversed only in the first two outcomes.

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures chosen only for illustration)

- **Notice window of 50 days:** an item posted on 2026-01-10 can be disputed with a qualifying notice dated up to 2026-03-01 (day 50); a notice dated 2026-03-02 falls outside.
- **Deadline of 3 business days, in a week with no Federal Reserve holiday:** notice given on Friday 2026-06-05. Day 1 is Monday 2026-06-08, day 3 is Wednesday 2026-06-10, so the credit is due from 2026-06-10 if the dispute is still submitted.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "a paid check can be disputed through this process". **Correct basis:** paid checks, wires and official checks are outside it.
- **Wrong reading:** "a second provisional credit can be posted if the first was too small". **Correct basis:** each dispute receives at most one provisional credit.

superseded_clauses: The provisional credit amount is the dispute's claimed_amount, but never more than the disputed item's amount.
